items.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 13 at 3:02AM PST until November 15 at 10:00AM PST by NWS San Diego CA
items.description:
...HIGH SURF ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT FROM 4 PM THIS AFTERNOON
TO 10 AM PST SUNDAY...

* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, cloud to ground
lightning expected as a band of thunderstorms moves ashore. For
the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5 to 7 feet
with sets to 8 to 9 feet at west facing beaches. High rip
current risk.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, until 8 AM PST this
morning. For the High Surf Advisory, from 4 PM this afternoon
to 10 AM PST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Cloud to ground lightning is expected at beaches
through 8 AM. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The thunderstorms and lightning threat will
diminish after 8 AM. Tides will be falling during this time, but
adjusted high tides will be near 7 feet which could combine with
the high surf to produce localized beach erosion and overflow
into parking lots and boardwalks. Surf begins to wane Sunday
afternoon but may remain elevated for west-facing beaches into
Monday.
items.instruction:
A beach hazards statement for beach lightning means that there is
the potential for cloud to ground or cloud to water lightning
strikes which could result in injury or death. Move indoors until
the storm passes and stay away from metal objects.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

items.headline: Special Marine Warning issued November 13 at 2:29AM PST until November 13 at 4:30AM PST by NWS San Diego CA
items.description:
SMWSGX

The National Weather Service in San Diego has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal Waters from San Mateo Point to the Mexican Border and out
to 10 nm...
Waters from San Mateo point to the Mexican Border Extending 10 to
60 nm out including San Clemente Island...

* Until 430 AM PST.

* At 227 AM PST, strong thunderstorms were located along a line
extending from 16 nm east of Avalon to 36 nm southwest of Point
Loma, moving east at 10 knots. This line of storms will continue
to move east to the coast of San Diego County through 5 AM.

HAZARD...Wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Small craft could be damaged in briefly higher winds and
suddenly higher waves.

* Strong thunderstorms will remain over mainly open waters.
items.instruction: Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

items.headline: Small Craft Advisory issued November 13 at 2:02AM PST until November 14 at 4:00PM PST by NWS San Diego CA
items.description:
* WHAT...Seas 5 to 9 ft and west winds 20 to 25 knots will lead
to choppy seas and dangerous boating conditions.

* WHERE...Coastal Waters from San Mateo Point to the Mexican
Border and out to 10 nm and Waters from San Mateo Point to the
Mexican Border Extending 10 to 60 nm out including San
Clemente Island.

* WHEN...From 10 AM today to 4 PM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Conditions will be hazardous to small craft.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Strongest winds will occur between 8 PM
tonight and 10 AM Saturday. Seas and winds will begin to
diminish Saturday afternoon, but seas may remain above 7 feet
into early Sunday, especially south of San Clemente Island.
items.instruction:
Inexperienced mariners, especially those operating smaller
vessels, should avoid navigating in hazardous conditions.

items.headline: Marine Weather Statement issued November 13 at 1:37AM PST by NWS San Diego CA
items.description:
A band of showers and isolated thunderstorms will move through the
coastal waters through about 8 AM this morning.

Any thunderstorm that forms will be capable of producing gusty,
erratic winds, choppy seas, lightning, and briefly heavy rainfall
with reduced visibility.
